para. 2: board shall report its findings to the President within thirty days

propositions.claim: The held text is the Federal Register printing of EO 10888 at 25 FR 9361.
propositions.quote: Title 3— THE PRESIDENT Executive Order 10888 CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE

propositions.claim: The order creates a three-member board to investigate the dispute.
propositions.quote: I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate this dispute.

propositions.claim: The board must report to the President within thirty days.
propositions.quote: The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.

propositions.claim: The status-quo command runs only until thirty days after the board's report.
propositions.quote: from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made

propositions.claim: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the Executive Orders it lists, with their amendments.
propositions.quote: it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:

propositions.claim: EO 12553's list names 10888 (line 292 of the held text, between 10878 and 10904).
The board was Emergency Board No. 133 and its report cover is dated December 10, 1960.
propositions.quote: APPOINTED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER 10888 DATED SEPTEMBER 28, 1960 ... WASHINGTON, D.C. DECEMBER 10, 1960 (Emergency Board No. 133)

propositions.claim: The board submitted its report to the President by letter of transmittal dated December 10, 1960; thirty days later is January 9, 1961.
propositions.quote: The Emergency Board created by you on September 28, 1960, by Executive Order 10888 ... has the honor to submit herewith its report and recommendations

review.conclusion_reason: NO at the cutoff and formal revocation are upheld by EO 12553. February 25, 1986 is a verified express ending, but not an established first operative ending: reporting was completed in 1960 and the status-quo command expired in 1961. The record does not establish whether any residual board function survived until revocation.
missed_evidence: NMB report, https://nmb.gov/NMB_Application/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/PEB-133-Report.pdf, PDF page 5 (printed page 1): 'the time for filing a report was extended to December 10, 1960' by the President with the parties' consent. This resolves the apparent reporting-deadline discrepancy.

verdicts.reason: Held official-printing OCR identifies EO 10888 and 25 FR 9361 and contains its text.
Original expressly creates a three-member board to investigate the dispute.
Original requires reporting within thirty days from the order date.
Original expressly limits the status-quo command to thirty days after reporting, subject to agreement.
Held EO 12553 expressly revokes the listed orders and their amendments; its date is February 25, 1986.
Line 292 of the held EO 12553 text lists 10888 between 10878 and 10904.
NMB report cover identifies EO 10888, Emergency Board No. 133, and December 10, 1960.
Report transmittal on PDF page 2 bears December 10, 1960 and submits the report to the President. Thirty days later is January 9, 1961.
The supplied finding aid repeats this disposition, but its API URL is truncated and the underlying OFR record was not independently opened.
